    Good representations are finite direct sums of intervals #

    Every E-good representation of I_* is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of the interval representations Y, A e, P e with e ∈ E. Together with IsGood.of_shortExact this gives Lemma 2.1, Step 2: extensions of objects of B_E lie in B_E.

    The proof splits off one interval at a time. If M(*) ≠ 0, a nonzero v ∈ M(*) survives up to a largest endpoint d ∈ E (or dies at once), and P d (or Y) splits off; otherwise a nonzero v ∈ M(0) gives a summand A d. Induction on dim M(*) + dim M(0) concludes.
